title: Probabilistic variance-aware throughput gate for PRs
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Summary:
Implement a probabilistic, variance-aware gating mechanism in the PR CI pipeline to detect performance regressions (tokens/sec and p95 latency) without blocking on noisy single-run samples. Current CI gates use fixed thresholds or single-run baselines which trigger false positives for high-variance workloads. This ticket adds an ensemble baseline model, Bayesian credible intervals for p95/tokens/sec, and an in-PR lightweight replay harness that runs multiple short micro-benchmarks to estimate the posterior distribution of relevant metrics. The gate should: (1) flag high-confidence regressions (>=95% posterior probability of degradation beyond a delta), (2) surface a risk score for medium-confidence changes (60-95%), and (3) allow auto-approval for small noise-level changes (<60% and within configured noise floor).

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- Create a synthetic micro-benchmark harness that can be executed in PR CI with <= 3 minutes wall time and <2x resource cost compared to unit tests.
- Implement Bayesian estimation over multiple runs to compute posterior for tokens/sec and p95 latency.
- Gate logic: block PRs when posterior probability of a regression (>=10% relative degradation for tokens/sec or >=10% increase for p95) is >=95%.
- Emit a human-readable risk breakdown in CI logs and link to a temporary Grafana snapshot showing run distributions.
- Add lightweight alerting (Slack/console) for repeated medium-confidence regressions to trigger follow-up investigation.
- Document the tuning knobs and how to interpret the risk score in the performance playbook.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace long-form, nightly baseline suites. It augments in-PR gating with probabilistic decisioning.

Implementation plan:
1) Design micro-benchmark suite (templated workloads representing common token length distributions and KV-cache hit patterns).
2) Build a small harness based on existing bench runners but constrained to run in parallel slices (N=3 short runs each with 30-60s samples).
3) Integrate a lightweight Bayesian estimator (conjugate priors for mean throughput, bootstrap for p95) implemented in Python to keep CI deps minimal.
4) Add gate step in PR pipeline that publishes artifacts and a risk verdict.
5) Add visualization: ephemeral Grafana dashboard links created from recorded traces stored in S3.
6) Run staging for 2 weeks behind a feature flag, review false positive/negative rate and tune priors/noise-floor.

Trade-offs considered:
- Bayesian estimates add compute and complexity; chosen because they reduce false positives compared to single-run thresholds.
- Conjugate priors simplify math but require reasonable prior calibration — we'll seed priors from the rolling nightly baseline.
- Using bootstrap for p95 is more computationally intensive but more robust to heavy-tailed distributions than assuming normality.

Links & Artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PR+Bayesian+Gate+Design
- Benchmark harness prototype (internal GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/86
- Example CI run (staging): https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/78321
- Grafana snapshot template: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/snapshots/pr-gate-template
- Performance playbook entry draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf/playbook/pr-gating

Operational notes:
- Default noise_floor set to 3% for tokens/sec and 5% for p95; these are configurable via pipeline variables.
- Run count: default 3 repeated slices per PR; will be tunable if CI time budget allows.
- Cost: estimated additional CI GPU time ~18 min per PR on average; plan to apply gating only on builds touching runtime/serving code or flagged by test heuristics.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): feature flag on, collect data for 2 weeks, manual review of all blocked PRs.
- Phase 2 (threshold tuning): adjust priors and noise_floor based on observed false-positive rate.
- Phase 3 (enforcement): enable blocking for >=95% regressions. Medium-confidence regressions create tickets automatically for perf team triage.

Monitoring & Metrics:
- Track gate outcomes (pass/flag/block) per PR, false-positive rate (post-merge reversals), median CI runtime increase, and average tokens/sec variance per workload.
- Dashboards: PR-gate outcomes, posterior distributions, and cumulative blocked PRs by author/area.
